code.originalText: Two-week review after starting replacement: electrolytes, cause, and autoimmune screening

text.paragraph: Two-week review after starting replacement: electrolytes, cause, and autoimmune screening. [S]

Ms. Austen returns two weeks after starting hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. She has missed no doses. Within three days the morning nausea stopped and her appetite returned, and she now eats three meals a day. The lightheadedness on standing has almost gone, and the salt craving is less. She is still tired by late afternoon but has started writing again for an hour each morning. Her back ache is milder. She has practised with the trainer kit and can recite the sick-day rules. She has not yet ordered the medical ID. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-02; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Brighter; weight 53.4 kg; blood pressure 108/68 seated
Pigmentation of the face, hands and gums unchanged so far

About three months of increasing tiredness, loss of 5 kg, darkening of the skin, nausea with bouts of vomiting, low back ache, salt craving and lightheadedness on standing, with low sodium, high potassium and raised eosinophils; adrenal insufficiency suspected and urgent endocrinology testing booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; its timing echoes the documented break in her health (D).

Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease): no cortisol response to cosyntropin with a markedly raised ACTH, and mineralocorticoid deficiency with raised renin and low aldosterone; on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the historical cause of her illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).
Mild normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL) with normal ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate
S — Synthetic finding at intake; it recovers on replacement.

list.item:
Primary adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune Addison's disease) (E27.1). 21-hydroxylase antibodies are positive (24 U/mL), so the cause is autoimmune adrenalitis; adrenal imaging and tuberculosis testing are not needed. She is responding well: nausea gone, weight up 1.6 kg, sodium 137 and potassium 4.6 mmol/L. Afternoon tiredness at two weeks is expected and does not by itself call for a higher dose. [S]
Continue hydrocortisone 10 mg and 5 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg.
Order the medical ID today; sick-day rules stated back correctly.
Renin, electrolytes and blood count at the six-week visit.

Mild normocytic anemia (D64.9). Hemoglobin 11.9 g/dL, rising; eosinophils back to normal on hydrocortisone. [S]
Blood count again at six weeks.
